newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end sluggish session mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end sluggish session mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed after a sluggish session.
"It was quiet all day," one analyst said of activity during the session.
While the mark and Swiss franc came under pressure in what some analysts called a correction after Wednesday's steep rises, sterling impressively held on to gains.
Moderate U.K. inflation data revealed in the retail price inflation report underpinned sentiment that U.K. rates could be headed higher, which provided support to sterling, the analyst said.

Trade was cautious, however, at the start of the EU summit in Dublin where European finance ministers are meeting to try to resolve differences on a pact to ensure fiscal discipline after the EU lauches its single currency in 1999.
U.S. economic data released this morning, which showed continued growth amid low inflation, had little impact on the market, analysts noted.
U.S. debt and stock markets firmed a bit after the release of the data, which weighed on currencies slightly after weak U.S. asset markets bolstered foreign exchange futures on Wednesday.

U.S. November retail sales fell 0.4 percent compared to expectations for a 0.3 percent rise, the consumer price index rose 0.3 percent versus an expected 0.2 percent rise, the Atlanta Fed diffusion index was at minus 3.3 versus minus 8.8 in October and November real earnings rose 1.0 percent.

At settlement, March yen futures fell $0.000030 to $0.008938, marks were off $0.0021 to $0.6519, Swiss francs fell 0.0022 to $0.7677, sterling was up $0.0052 to $1.6532, the Canadian dollar was up $0.0018 at $0.7411, the Australian dollar was up $0.0025 to $0.7917 and the peso eased $0.000325 to $0.119750.
